newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU plans to protect financial services consumers.
newsitem.headline: EU plans to protect financial services consumers.

text.p: The European Commission will announce on Thursday a list of new legislation it is planning to improve consumer protection in the financial services sector.
"It's a sort of action plan announcing what we plan to do to enhance consumer confidence...in financial services," a European Commission spokesperson said.
Among the new legislation will be a directive in the area of distance contracts in financial services, where the Commission intends to submit a proposal by the autumn.

Under the plan, a follow-up to a green paper unveiled last year by the two Italian Commissioners Mario Monti and Emma Bonino, the Commission would also by early 1998 propose a directive to regulate intermediaries for financial services.
It also proposes to create legislation for motor insurance, covering accidents outside a motorist's own country, and to update existing legislation regulating intermediaries in the insurance sector.

In other areas, like mortgage credit and new forms of payment like screen banking the Commission intends to concentrate on information campaigns and securing transparency, rather than by proposing binding legislation, the spokesperson said.
